title: The axioms supply no dark sector, and the "taste cube" that would host one is an unclosed bridge
plain: The four axioms say nothing about what dark matter is. The dark-matter notes borrow a larger structure, a cube of eight "taste" states meant to carry Standard Model charges, and call two of the eight dark. The bridge from the axioms to that cube is itself on the axiom memo's list of open gates. So the framework has no derived answer yet to "what is dark matter".

title: The notes give the dark state incompatible charges, and offer three mutually exclusive dark candidates
plain: Different dark-matter notes describe different particles. One says the dark particle feels no force but gravity, is Planck-mass, and cannot be tested. Another treats it as a 3.9 TeV particle that annihilates through a gauge-like force, and its mass derivation needs it to carry colour charge. A third calls a right-handed neutrino the "DM candidate", though that particle decays in about 10^-30 seconds. These cannot all hold.

title: The dark mass 16 v was found by scanning against the abundance target, and no mechanism exists
plain: The dark mass, 16 times the electroweak scale (3.94 TeV), was found by searching a list of framework numbers for one that makes the observed baryon asymmetry come out. Every attempt to explain why the mass should be 16 v has failed, been corrected, or stayed a numerical coincidence. So the mass is a fit to the answer, not a prediction.

title: The annihilation force and the coupling in the Sommerfeld factor are chosen, not derived
plain: How much dark matter survives depends on how strongly it annihilates. The notes pick the coupling from a range: 0.03 to 0.05 in one note, about 0.091 to 0.092 in others, and these give different answers. A dark particle that feels no gauge force would not have that coupling at all. The resulting dark-to-ordinary ratio comes out 1.5 to 2% above the measured 5.36.

title: R = R_base x S is a group-theory identity presented as the physical dark-to-baryon density ratio
plain: The number 31/9 is exact arithmetic on group-theory constants. Nothing shows why the real ratio of dark to ordinary matter should equal it. The lane's own earlier note showed that ordinary matter is left over from a matter-antimatter imbalance, not from annihilation freeze-out, so a ratio of annihilation strengths cannot give it. Later notes reuse the number to compute the imbalance.

title: The baryon asymmetry eta is imported, and both derivation routes are blocked
plain: The lane needs the amount of ordinary matter, which comes from the matter-antimatter imbalance eta, and takes it from observation. The neutrino route to eta gives 0.19 of the observed value. Reaching 1.0 needs a neutrino-phase sign that no note can derive, and about thirty notes close the alternative routes. The old electroweak route stalls on undetermined inputs.

title: The thermal, cosmic-history substrate of a relic abundance is imported
plain: A relic abundance is a statement about a hot, expanding early universe cooling past a freeze-out point. The axioms give no time metric, no expansion law, no thermal state and no starting condition. The framework's cosmology inputs (Friedmann law, particle count, today's temperature, freeze-out constant) are imported or conditional, and the repo's current rule is that an unresolved cosmology input supplies no premise.
